You are a hardware-debug reviewer. A first debug agent diagnosed an RISC-V RTL failure and an explain.png diagram was drawn from that diagnosis (explain.png sha256 first 16 hex: 7122fe5e95e4ff3f).
Case: picosoc-uart-div
Failing trace window (same window the first diagnosis saw):
- tb_picosoc_uart seed 43
- divider 64 loopback send 0xa5
tohost: FAIL 0xdead
TRAP: uart data mismatch got 0xe0 want 0xa5
CYCLES=2112
- /home/tuncay/afterglow/sim/tb/picosoc-uart-div_tb.sv:86: Verilog $finish
- S i m u l a t i o n   R e p o r t: Verilator 5.052 2026-09-05
- Verilator: $finish at 21ns; walltime 0.001 s; speed 42.140 us/s
- Verilator: cpu 0.001 s on 1 threads; allocated 4 MB
First diagnosis (verbatim):
Loopback divider 64 sent 0xa5 but recv_buf_data returned 0xe0 (TRAP: uart data mismatch got 0xe0 want 0xa5, FAIL 0xdead). Both data/stop states test recv_divcnt > (cfg_divider >> 4) so bits are sampled after ~4 cycles instead of a full cfg_divider period, causing bit-slip from 0xa5 to 0xe0. Fix restores full-bit wait to cfg_divider in both states. Refs picosoc/simpleuart.v:20, picosoc/picosoc.v:190.
First patch_diff:
diff --git a/picosoc/simpleuart.v b/picosoc/simpleuart.v
--- a/picosoc/simpleuart.v
+++ b/picosoc/simpleuart.v
@@ -89,14 +89,14 @@
 				10: begin
-					if (recv_divcnt > (cfg_divider >> 4)) begin
+					if (recv_divcnt > cfg_divider) begin
 						recv_buf_data <= recv_pattern;
 						recv_buf_valid <= 1;
 						recv_state <= 0;
 					end
 				end
 				default: begin
-					if (recv_divcnt > (cfg_divider >> 4)) begin
+					if (recv_divcnt > cfg_divider) begin
 						recv_pattern <= {ser_rx, recv_pattern[7:1]};
 						recv_state <= recv_state + 1;
 						recv_divcnt <= 0;
 					end
 				end
Look at the diagram (explain.png in the run bundle) together with the trace above. Either CONFIRM the first diagnosis (it explains the failing signal and the diff fixes it) or REVISE it (it misnames the signal or the diff is wrong). Reply JSON ONLY with keys: decision (exactly "CONFIRM" or "REVISE"), diagnosis (final diagnosis text), patch_diff (final unified diff), reason (one sentence: why the diagram confirms or what it corrects).
